text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.7% today as oil prices tumbled below $100 per barrel, driven by optimism that the U.S. might negotiate with Iran rather than escalate further. While Middle East tensions remain serious—the Strait of Hormuz is closed, the Saudi East-West pipeline is shut down, and attacks continue—the market is pricing in potential relief from diplomatic talks, which would ease the supply squeeze that had been supporting higher prices.

The stock has now dropped 4.4% over two weeks as the oil market swung from fearing severe supply disruption to hoping for negotiated resolution. Even though real supply constraints persist (Saudi pipeline down, Iranian shipments disrupted), the *possibility* of a deal was enough to shift trader sentiment and pull crude prices lower, directly weighing on a company whose earnings depend on oil price strength.
